questions.question: Which Guru compiled the Adi Granth, the first version of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Adi Granth, gathering the bani of the earlier Gurus along with his own and that of the Bhagats.

questions.question: Mundavani, near the close of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji ('In this dish are placed three things: Truth, Contentment and Wisdom'), was composed by which Guru?
questions.explanation: In the Mundavani, Guru Arjan Dev Ji sums up the nature of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, likening it to a dish holding Truth, Contentment and Wisdom.

questions.question: In 1604, where was the Adi Granth first installed (Parkash)?
questions.explanation: Guru Arjan Dev Ji installed the Adi Granth at Sri Harmandir Sahib in August 1604.

questions.question: Who was appointed the first Granthi of Sri Harmandir Sahib when the Adi Granth was installed?
questions.explanation: At the first Parkash in 1604, Guru Arjan Dev Ji appointed Baba Buddha Ji as the first Granthi.

questions.question: The bani of which Guru was added by Guru Gobind Singh Ji at Damdama Sahib to complete Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji added the bani of his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, to the Granth; Bhai Mani Singh Ji wrote this version.

questions.question: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh Ji bestow eternal Guruship (Gurgaddi) on Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: In 1708 at Nanded (Hazur Sahib), Guru Gobind Singh Ji declared that the Granth would be the Guru after him.
questions.source: Basics of Sikhi: Guru Granth Sahib Ji

questions.question: How many Angs (pages) does the standard Saroop of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji have?
questions.explanation: The standard Saroop of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji has 1430 Angs, ending with Raagmala on Angs 1429-1430.

questions.question: Into how many main Raags is the bani of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji arranged?
questions.explanation: Of the many Raags and Raginis, the Gurus used 31 main Raags to arrange the bani of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
questions.note: Some count 60+ including mixed forms; question says 'main Raags'.

questions.question: Which Raag opens the Raag section of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji (from Ang 14)?
questions.explanation: The Raag section begins on Ang 14 with Sri Raag and ends with Raag Jaijavanti.
questions.source: Sikhs.org: Arrangement and Layout of SGGS

questions.question: With which words does the Mool Mantar begin?
questions.explanation: The Mool Mantar, the basic creed at the opening of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, begins 'Ik Oankar, Sat Naam, Karta Purakh, Nirbhau, Nirvair...'.
questions.source: Sikh Rehat Maryada (English translation) – Asia Samachar

questions.question: Which composition appears at the very end of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji (Angs 1429-1430)?
questions.explanation: Raagmala, an index of musical measures, is the final composition, following the Mundavani on Ang 1429.
questions.source: Sikhs.org: Arrangement and Layout of SGGS

questions.question: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji contains the bani of how many Sikh Gurus?
questions.explanation: It contains the bani of the first five Gurus and the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

questions.question: Which Guru contributed the largest number of hymns to Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Arjan Dev Ji contributed the most hymns (2,218 by the SGPC's count), followed by Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

questions.question: Among the Bhagats, whose bani has the largest share in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Kabir Ji has the largest number of hymns among the Bhagats included in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

questions.question: Sheikh Farid, whose Shaloks are included in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, belonged to which tradition?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Farid was a Sufi mystic of the Chishti order and the first recorded poet of Punjabi; his shabads and shaloks are in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
questions.note: Count of Farid's shaloks varies; not asked.

questions.question: Bhagat Namdev Ji, whose hymns are in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, is also famous for devotional poetry in which language?
questions.explanation: Namdev was a medieval poet-saint who wrote Marathi abhangas; some of his verses are included in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

questions.question: In which script is Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji written?
questions.explanation: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji is written in Gurmukhi script, though its hymns use several languages including Punjabi, Braj, Persian and Sanskrit.
questions.source: Sikhs.org: Arrangement and Layout of SGGS

questions.question: An Akhand Path, the continuous reading of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji by a relay of readers, takes about how long?
questions.explanation: An Akhand Path is a non-stop recitation by a relay of readers, completed in about 48 hours.

questions.question: What is the ceremony called when Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji is respectfully closed and put to rest, usually in the evening?
questions.explanation: Sukhasan is the evening ceremony of putting Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji to rest; Parkash is the morning opening ceremony.

questions.question: The Savaiye in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, composed in praise of the Gurus, were written by which group of poets?
questions.explanation: The Bhatts, a group of bards, composed the Savaiye, near the end of the Granth, praising the Gurus.
questions.source: Basics of Sikhi: Guru Granth Sahib Ji
questions.note: Number of Bhatts (11 vs 17) is disputed; not asked.
